persona.label: Rushed but qualified
persona.description: Busy professional between meetings. Terse, answers several things at once. Should be transferred.
persona.behavior: You are between meetings and have about five minutes. Your first reply says something like "ok but make it fast, I'm busy." Use short, lowercase texts with no pleasantries. When asked something, answer it, and volunteer one or two related facts if it saves time. Round numbers the way people do ("about 520", "owe like 310k"). If the assistant is slow or repetitive, show mild impatience. You want a lower rate and you want to talk to someone today.

transcript.text: Hi Taylor, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
ok but make it fast, i'm busy. looking to lower my rate, currently at 7.25
Got it, I'll keep this quick. Roughly what's your home worth right now, and about how much do you still owe on the mortgage?

objections.rationale: The borrower said "ok but make it fast, i'm busy," which already consented to texting. The agent respected that with "Got it, I'll keep this quick" and asked only the essential questions, combining value and balance into one message. It never offered the playbook's callback-time option, but given the borrower's explicit go-ahead, the omission was low-impact.

judge.naturalness_rationale: The messages are brief, warm and adapted to a busy borrower. Turn 2 combines two questions into one message. Turn 4 adds a short reassurance ("this question doesn't involve a credit check"). Turn 6 opens with the borrower's name and answers the request to talk today directly, without filler.
judge.experience_rationale: Taylor wanted speed, got three quick exchanges and was routed immediately at turn 6. The agent explained who will call ("a licensed loan officer"), how ("at this number") and when ("usually within 5 minutes"), and set the honest expectation that they "may confirm a few details."
judge.handoff_summary_rationale: The summary accurately captures every figure the borrower gave: $520k value, $310k balance, 7.25% current rate, primary residence and 740+ credit. It records the ASAP timeline and the borrower's busy preference, and computes LTV correctly (~0.596). The recommended next step is actionable and tells the loan officer to keep it efficient.

annotations.note: The agent discloses up front that it is "an automated assistant," names the inquiry source, and offers STOP.
"Got it, I'll keep this quick" acknowledges the time pressure, and the message combines home value and balance into one question.
The agent did not offer the playbook's callback-time alternative for a busy borrower, though the borrower had already agreed to proceed by text.
"This question doesn't involve a credit check" heads off a common worry while collecting the credit band in a single tap-style list.
The handoff message says who, how and when ("licensed loan officer," "at this number," "usually within 5 minutes") without quoting rates or implying approval.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, fast, compliant qualification and handoff that fits a busy borrower's request. The only minor gap is not offering a callback option at the busy objection.
